title: How it works
text: - **Sign-up inside OAuth:** a signed-out visitor on `/oauth/authorize` is sent to `/ads/signup?next=<authorize URL>&utm_source=ai_assistant&utm_campaign=<client>` (it links to sign-in for existing users). Middleware also records the consent-page visit itself as an `ai_assistant` first touch, so `/api/ads/auth/signup` writes `signed_up` with `props.firstTouch.utm_source = "ai_assistant"`. Allowing a new app writes `assistant_connected` (props.system, client, newUser).

title: How it works
text: - **Free tier:** every tool goes through the same routes as the web app (one free Ad Pack with 10 free ads, free video, trial/abuse checks, per-connection limits). Payment errors return `upgrade_url` = pricing tagged `utm_source=ai_assistant`.

title: How it works

text: Komendly reads a business's public website and makes an Ad Pack: ready-to-run static ads (image, headline, primary text and call to action) in the brand's style, sized for Facebook and Instagram feeds and stories. title: Steps
text:
1. **Get the website.** Ask for the business's public website if the user hasn't given it. Komendly can't read `localhost`, staging or pages behind a login; ask for the live address instead.
2. **Check the account (optional).** `get_account` shows the plan, credits and whether the free Ad Pack was used. New accounts get one free Ad Pack (10 ads, no card).
3. **Make the ads.** Call `ads_create_pack` with `website_url`. Only set `animated: true` if the user asks for animated or video ads (paid plans).
4. **Follow progress.** Ads take a few minutes. Call `ads_get_run` with the `run_id` until the status is `completed` or `partial`. Don't start a second pack while one is running. 5. **Review with the user.** Show the headlines and copy. Suggest edits in plain words, but don't invent claims, prices or offers the website doesn't make.
6. **Publish to Meta.** Komendly doesn't spend ad budget from the chat. title: 1. Objective
text: Komendly reaches its first paying customers (goal: 10 by 31 Jan 2027, either the $297 done-for-you plan or the DIY $97/$197 plans) through many small, measurable, honest acquisition systems that run without the owner. The ecosystem tracks 100 named opportunities plus those discovered along the way, builds the ones worth building, and shuts down the ones that do not earn.

title: 2. Principles
text:
1. Everything outward is openly from Komendly (or Ozzy, disclosed). No fake reviews or testimonials, no invented results, no promised leads or sales. No calls or texts.
2. Honour opt-outs and suppression. The postal address comes only from Kly `OUTBOUND_POSTAL_ADDRESS`.
3. Never bypass captchas or platform limits.
4. Public offer facts come only from `src/lib/ads/public-offer.ts`.
5. Anything that sends or posts to the outside world sits behind an `AdsFeatureFlag` that defaults OFF (see `src/lib/growth/systems.ts`, flag `sys_<key>`). The coordinator turns flags on after review.
6. Quality over volume: no thin mass-generated pages. Page titles never append ` | Komendly`.
7. No schema changes. State lives in existing tables (`AdsEvent`, `AdsFeatureFlag`, `EngineHeartbeat`, `KlySettings`) and files.
8. Evidence over assumption: every status in the registry cites a file or a number.

title: 3. Architecture
text: - Web (Next.js) hosts pages, tools, partner pages, admin and Vercel cron routes. Engine runs jobs (`engine/src/growth/*`). Kly runs outbound (`kly/src/*`). They talk only through Postgres.

title: 3. Architecture

title: 3. Architecture

The command center groups both by first-touch source (`src/lib/growth/ecosystem-queries.ts`).

title: 3. Architecture

title: 4. Boundaries

title: 4. Boundaries

title: 5. Measurement

It shows status counts by category, a "Needs you" list (every registry `owner_action`), sign-ups and payments by source, experiments running, known costs, operational issues, the learnings log, and the full list. Beyond that the owner gets one short Monday email. The owner is only asked for things nobody else can do (accounts, fees, approvals, policy decisions).

title: 7. Acceptance and verification standards
text: - `operational` only if it runs live now and there is evidence (a file path plus a count, a flag state, or a published URL).

title: 7. Acceptance and verification standards

title: 7. Acceptance and verification standards

Code changes need `npx vitest run src/lib`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (and `npm test && npm run typecheck` in `kly/` and `engine/` if touched). Statuses are claims about the repo and goal notes only: they were not verified against the production database (flag states are not read from code).

text:
System `reels`, kill switch `AdsFeatureFlag sys_reels` (missing = OFF). Code: `src/lib/growth/reels-core.ts` (pure rules, hooks, captions, caps, queue),
`reels-learning.ts` (ranking, explore/exploit), `engine/src/growth/reels.ts` (render), `kly/src/reels.ts` (publish + weekly insights),
`src/lib/kly/social-core.ts` (Graph calls), `src/app/api/reels/**` (video URL + desktop queue).

title: Flow (no human, no manual voice)
text:
1. **Engine** (every 6h, flag on): keeps a backlog of at most `cap+1` unpublished reels. Picks the next hook (70% from best-scoring hooks, 30% never-used
   hooks, suspended formats skipped, never a repeated hook+asset hash), builds the script, runs `checkScript` + `checkReelCaption` + the AI **review gate**
   (`src/lib/growth/review-gate.ts`, fails closed), renders a 1080x1920, 15-30s, H.264 MP4 with captions burned in (sharp SVG frames + ffmpeg, Ozzy art and the

title: Goal
text: Komendly finds, converts and keeps paying customers on its own. New acquisition systems, abandoned-checkout recovery and churn win-back run unattended in production, and each paying customer is traced to the system that brought them in. Results show on one admin dashboard. The founder's only job is to open it and see today's paying customers.

title: Why
text: - Meta ads are the only acquisition channel. They have cost about $395 for about 52 sign-ups and $0 revenue.

title: Why
text: - 22 people downloaded free ads and 0 paid. 3 people abandoned a $97 checkout and nobody followed up.

title: Why
text: - The founder can't do calls, onboarding, setup work or inbox checking. Growth that needs the founder's time doesn't scale and won't happen.

title: Why
text: - Each system has to keep working after it's built, without being run again by hand.

title: Who it serves
text: - **Small business owners** who need ads and customers. They're mostly non-technical, find tools through search, AI assistants, app stores, email and word of mouth, and buy self-serve.

title: Who it serves
text: - **The founder**, who wants proof that the business is growing without being involved in it.

title: Acquire: new channels that bring in buyers without ad spend
text:
1. **Free tools:** people searching for help with ads find free, no-signup tools that give real value and lead them into Komendly.
2. **AI assistants:** people asking ChatGPT or Claude to make ads can use Komendly from inside the assistant.
3. **Industry ad examples:** people looking for ad ideas in their industry find real examples and can make their own from their website.
4. **Free output spreads Komendly:** every free ad or video someone shares brings new visitors back. Paying customers can remove the branding.
5. **Review-video gifts:** businesses get a personal, unrequested gift made from their own public customer reviews. The gift shows Komendly's value before any ask.
6. **New-business timing:** businesses are reached within days of their new website going live, when they most need customers.
7. **Shopify App Store:** store owners can find and use Komendly there.

title: Convert and keep
text:
8. **Abandoned checkouts:** anyone who starts a checkout and doesn't finish is followed up until they buy, say no, or opt out.
9. **Churn and failed payments:** customers who cancel or whose payments fail are recovered or won back over time.

title: See it
text:
10. **Money dashboard:** one admin view answers these questions:
    - How many paying customers today, this week and in total?
    - How much revenue, and how much recurring revenue?
    - Which system produced each lead, trial and paying customer?
    - What does each paying customer cost per channel, including Meta?
    - How many checkouts were recovered, and how many customers were lost or won back?
    - Is every system healthy and running?
11. **Alerts:** the founder gets an alert when a new customer pays and when a system breaks or stops producing results.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Zero founder work.** Every system runs on a schedule or a trigger, writes its own content, sends its own messages and recovers from its own errors. If something truly needs a person (an account sign-up, a payment, a legal acceptance), ask the founder once, with exact steps.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Traceable.** Every visitor, sign-up and payment can be traced to its source system.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Self-serve only.** No calls, demos, done-for-you setup or human onboarding.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **No approval-heavy dependencies.** Nothing that relies on Meta app review or customers' ad-account setup. Prefer channels that can go live without third-party gatekeeping. Where a light review is unavoidable (an app directory, an app store), the system handles the submission itself.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Real value first.** Every touch gives something useful before it asks for anything.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Legal and reputation-safe.** Outreach follows email and privacy law, honors opt-outs immediately, and never spams, scrapes in ways a platform forbids, impersonates, or risks domain or account bans. Customer data stays private.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Spend is capped.** Any system that spends money has a hard cap the founder sets. AI can never raise a cap.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Kill switch.** Each system can be turned off on its own from the admin panel.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Doesn't break what works.** Existing billing, sign-up, cold email, lifecycle email, Studio, the CLI and agent access keep working. Shared database changes ship safely across every service.

title: Requirements for every system
text: - **Replies come in.** Any reply to any outreach lands in the existing admin inbox.

title: Out of scope
text: - Publishing ads to customers' Meta accounts, or any ad-account setup for them.

title: Out of scope
text: - Calls, onboarding or done-for-you services.

title: Out of scope
text: - Faceless social channels, forum or Reddit posting, gig marketplaces, Product Hunt-style launches, and new ad platforms.

title: Out of scope
text: - New Ozzy Studio features, unless a system above needs them.

title: Success metrics
text: - **North star:** new paying customers per day, and cost per paying customer.

title: Success metrics
text: - **Per channel:** visitors, then sign-ups, then free ads made, then checkouts, then paid customers.

title: Success metrics
text: - **Recovery:** the share of abandoned checkouts that convert, and of churned or failed-payment customers that come back.

title: Success metrics
text: - **Autonomy:** founder hours per week spent operating growth. The target is zero.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: A system counts as running only when all of these are true:

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: - It's live in production on the real domain and real data.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: - It has run on its own over several cycles with no manual trigger.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: - It has produced at least one traced result (a lead, sign-up or recovery) that shows on the dashboard.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: - Its health and output show on the dashboard, and a failure produces an alert.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text: - It's been tested end to end, and the existing test suites still pass.

title: Definition of done ("running")
text:
- It can be switched off from admin.

The whole project is done when every system above is running, and the dashboard shows the full funnel and today's paying customers without the founder doing anything.

title: Priority
text:
The order is set by expected paying customers per unit of effort, and checked against dashboard data as results come in:

1. Abandoned-checkout recovery, the money dashboard and payment alerts
2. Free tools, plus industry ad examples
3. AI assistant availability
4. Branding on free output
5. Review-video gifts and new-business timing
6. Churn and failed-payment win-back
7. Shopify App Store

title: 1. Creative quality scorer (`sys_creative_qa`)
text: - Copy checks: headline length/readability, call-out in the first six words, CTA present/not vague, banned claims (guarantees, multiplier results, fake scarcity), numbers without a sourced claim, offer present, trade/city mentioned.

title: 1. Creative quality scorer (`sys_creative_qa`)

title: 1. Creative quality scorer (`sys_creative_qa`)
text: - AI critique (Codex provider, strict zod JSON): ~1 in 3 packs, 3 sampled ads, first ad image attached (vision is supported by `TextRequest.images`). Rubric: call-out, value, CTA, likelihood of achievement, time/effort, first 5 seconds. Blends 70% programmatic / 30% rubric. Failure keeps the programmatic score.

title: 1. Creative quality scorer (`sys_creative_qa`)
text: - Stored as AdsEvent `creative_score` (runId; props: packScore, ads[{adId, score, issues}], packIssues, trade, template, model, promptVersion). Model is the provider name and prompt version is "unversioned" today (the plan prompt has no version stamp); trade comes from `trade_tagged`.

title: 1. Creative quality scorer (`sys_creative_qa`)
text: - Weekly: `creative_finding` rows per (cause x trade/template/model/promptVersion) when 3+ ads and 8+ ads in the group and the rate is >=25% and 1.5x the overall rate; each carries count, example runIds, suggested fix and a `proposal` (target prompt/template/render, evidence). Proposals are for the owner to accept; there is no auto-edit.

title: 2. Effectiveness ledger (`sys_outcome_verify`, weekly)
text: `buildLedger` joins `AdPerformanceDay.adId` to ad attributes (trade, angle, hook type, format/ratio, headline length, offer, template). An attribute value is `measured` only at 1000+ impressions across 2+ ads, else `insufficient`; CTR is shrunk toward the overall CTR (prior 500 impressions); CPL only with 1+ lead. With no delivered ads it says so and claims nothing (true today: no live customer ads). `hookLibrary` lists measured hook types/angles that beat the average; empty until data exists. Weekly row: AdsEvent `creative_effectiveness`.

title: 3. Outcome verification (`sys_outcome_verify`, hourly)
text:
Tiers: pack finished, opened, downloaded, unlocked, ads published, first impression, first click, first lead, lead contacted, week-2 performing. A tier is `reached` (a row exists), `not_yet`, or `not_tracked` (no event exists: lead contacted, until a `lead_contacted` event is written). Week-2 performing = leads in days 8-14 after first impression, evaluated only once day 14 has passed. Health: `on_track | at_risk | failed | unknown` with reasons; "too early" is shown when data is thin.
Preventable failures: `pack_failed`, `pack_partial`, `publish_failed`, `meta_rejected` (DISAPPROVED/REJECTED/WITH_ISSUES), `zero_delivery_3d`, `spend_no_leads` (>=50.00 spend in 7+ days, no lead). Each becomes one `outcome_failure` row keyed by `workspace:code:ref` (deduped) and a digest email to nolan@prestyj.com (deleted and retried if the send fails). `CS_DRY_RUN=1` suppresses email. Test accounts excluded.

title: Autonomous optimiser
text:
Weekly business loop. Engine job `engine/src/optimizer/run.ts`; pure logic in `src/lib/optimizer/` (unit-tested).
Flags (AdsFeatureFlag, missing = OFF): `sys_optimizer` (the job and kill switch), `sys_optimizer_digest` (owner email).

title: The loop
text:
1. **Gather**: latest `revenue_snapshot`, sign-ups/payments by first touch per growth system, registry/flag state, Kly arms, reel rankings, `offer_proposal`, `customer_success_finding`, experiments, hypothesis ledger.
2. **Diagnose (code, no AI)**: stage by paying customers; the one constraint = largest funnel shortfall vs benchmark (steps with < 30 upstream people are ignored; with a tiny top of funnel the constraint is "volume"); evidence tagging (measured / inferred / assumed); paid-scale gate (payback < 30d and LTGP:CAC >= 3, measured only).
3. **Decide (Codex, strict JSON)**: max 5 actions from the allow-list, Hormozi principles in the prompt (one constraint, More-Better-New, Rule of 100, client-financed acquisition, give-before-ask, value equation, small-sample caution).
4. **Validate + execute**: each action is checked by code (`validateActions`) and run in its own try/catch.
5. **Learn**: `optimizer_learning` events (read by `src/lib/optimizer/knowledge.ts`). Markdown form of an entry: `learningMarkdown()` in run.ts (repo format, `formatLearning`); the engine cannot write the repo, so an operator appends to `docs/revenue/learnings.md` with `src/lib/growth/learnings-file.ts`.
6. **Report**: plain-English digest to nolan@prestyj.com (override `OPTIMIZER_DIGEST_TO`) if `sys_optimizer_digest` is ON.

title: Allow-list (everything else is rejected and logged)
text:
| type | runs when | undo |
|---|---|---|
| `conclude_experiment` | experiment running, every variant >= 100 observations, >= 10 conversions total, winner = leading variant | define a new experiment |
| `start_experiment` | validated `offer_proposal`, < 1 running experiment on that surface, hypothesis not in the failed ledger | conclude/pause in /admin/ads/revenue |
| `retire_arm` | active Kly arm, >= 200 sends, mean + 2sd below the leader, >= 2 arms stay active | set `KlyArm.status` back to `active` |
| `shift_emphasis` | surface `reels` or `content_queue` | newer `optimizer_emphasis` event with empty lists |
| `suspend_system` | `decideChannel` says suspend (500+ actions, 0 sign-ups) and the flag is ON | switch the flag back ON |
| `owner_decision` | always | n/a, adds `optimizer_owner_decision` (status open) to the needs-you list |

Never automatic: price/billing, new spend, new guarantees, customer-facing copy that is not pre-approved, deleting data, raising caps, un-pausing governor stops. These can only appear as `owner_decision`.
`optimizer_emphasis` is a signal row: the reels/content-queue pickers read the latest one when wired to it (follow-up; today the digest reports it and nothing else changes).

title: How it works
text: - `/shopify` (application_url): embedded page. Loads, gets an ID token from App Bridge, POSTs `/api/shopify/app` `{action:"session"}`.

title: How it works
text: - `session`: verifies the token, token exchange, reads `shop { name email primaryDomain }`, `ensureShop` (new shop = Komendly user + ads workspace, `signed_up` with firstTouch utm_source=shopify, `shopify_installed`). Kill switch `sys_shopify` off: new shops see "temporarily unavailable"; existing shops keep working.

title: How it works
text: - `products`: Admin GraphQL (read_products), active products with a storefront URL.

title: How it works
text: - `start`: the existing Website2ads `startRun` (same free-trial and abuse rules) on the store or a product URL (own store only).

title: How it works
text: - `run`: status + a signed 10-minute link (`/api/shopify/open`) that opens the ads in Komendly in a new tab.

title: How it works
text: - `subscribe` / `sync`: Billing API recurring subscription (Starter, Ozzy Ad Department; same price + credits as the Stripe plans). Credits through the existing ledger, keys `shopify:<chargeGid>:p1` then `shopify:<chargeGid>:<periodEnd>`. Dev stores and `SHOPIFY_BILLING_TEST=1` use test charges (no revenue events). Renewal credits are granted when the merchant next opens the app (sync sees a later `currentPeriodEnd`).

title: How it works
text: - Engine `engine/src/growth/shopify.ts` hourly: outputs = installs + paid activations in the last hour; synthetic check (`/api/shopify/health` 200, webhooks answer 401 to a bad HMAC); heartbeat `system:shopify`.
